name: Alila Shanghai
positioning: Alila's first urban outpost in China, in Shanghai's historic Jing'an district overlooking the Zhangyuan Shikumen compound, with interiors inspired by Chinese courtyard homes and old Shanghai's shikumen houses
best_for: Travelers who want a calm, design-led base in central Shanghai
Guests interested in wellness and hands-on Chinese cultural experiences

facts.text: Alila Shanghai is at 500 Weihai Road in Shanghai's historic Jing'an district.
The hotel overlooks the historic Zhangyuan Shikumen compound.
The hotel is within walking distance or a short drive of Shanghai Grand Theatre, People's Park and Shanghai Museum, and close to Nanjing Road shopping.
Alila Shanghai is Alila's first urban outpost in China.
Interiors by Beijing-based designer Ju Bin riff on traditional Chinese courtyard homes and the East-meets-West style of old Shanghai's shikumen houses.
Design elements throughout the rooms celebrate Chinese craftsmanship and culture while embodying Shanghai's blend of modernity and tradition.
Rooms have natural finishes and a spa-like bathroom with Shanghai-inspired detailing, from textured glass to bold floor tiles.
The Penthouse Suite is on the hotel's highest floor.
Spa Alila blends modern healing therapies with traditional Eastern practices, offering massages, facials, herbal scrubs and body wraps.
A library on the Lobby Level holds a curated collection of books on Shanghai's history and culture.
500 Weihai Road is the hotel's Chinese restaurant, integrating seafood into traditional Shanghai cuisine with sustainable, seasonal ingredients.
Secret Roof serves coffee by day and handcrafted coffee cocktails by night, with views of historical Zhangyuan.

highlights.text: The fourth-floor lobby is a light-flooded courtyard in the sky, with pathways, waterworks and gardens around a ceramic and stainless steel tree sculpture by local artist Oscar Wang.
On Level 5, an indoor infinity pool overlooks the hotel's green garden, alongside a hydrotherapy pool and a wet sauna.
Shikumen View rooms overlook Zhangyuan's shikumen rooftops, and one room type adds a private terrace.
In-house guests can join a complimentary gong sound bath, one of the hotel's Alila Moments.
Another Alila Moment takes guests to Lei Yun Shang, a Chinese medicine clinic founded in 1734, for a personal consultation with a senior practitioner.

considerations.text: The hotel no longer provides bottled water or disposable in-room amenities, so guests are advised to bring their own essentials and a drinking vessel.
Views vary by floor and direction; only East-facing rooms on high floors glimpse The Bund's skyline on the horizon.
Guests must wear a swimming cap in the pool.
